mfg1-surface-completion37-lesson-001.title: Match anodized-coating tests to the properties assessed
mfg1-surface-completion37-lesson-001.objective: Separate corrosion, light resistance, wear, hardness and electrical assessments; distinguish test examples from product acceptance limits.

paragraphs.title: Comparing corrosion
paragraphs.text: Salt spray testing exposes specimens to a specified environment and examines corrosion. Other methods include alkaline-drop and copper-accelerated acetic acid salt spray (CASS) testing. CASS uses conditions containing copper salts. Different methods have different conditions and result scales; do not simply convert a short test into a long exposure.

paragraphs.title: Fading and wear are different
paragraphs.text: Light-resistance assessment of colored coatings may use xenon-arc or carbon-arc exposure. Rotary abrasion tests assess material lost through contact with abrasive wheels or similar bodies. Retaining color and resisting frictional wear are separate properties. Match the specified method, measured quantity and acceptance value; exposure time or revolutions alone cannot determine acceptance.

paragraphs.title: Read HV separately from withstand voltage
paragraphs.text: HV means Vickers hardness. A diamond pyramid makes an indentation; hardness relates the load to its surface area. Its top view has two diagonals and differs from an elongated Knoop indentation. Hardness, wear resistance and withstand voltage are different quantities. For thin coatings, consider substrate effects and whether the method is suitable.

paragraphs.title: Reference conditions do not establish current standards
paragraphs.text: Concentrations, durations, thicknesses, voltages and temperatures in the source are examples within that explanation. References to JIS H 8681 or JIS H 8685 do not verify the current edition. For actual products, confirm the specified edition, product requirements and the test specialist’s assessment. Typical coating values do not guarantee protection from electric shock or a heating limit.

terms.meaning: Resistance to light-induced discoloration or fading.

terms.reading: かいてんまもうしけん
terms.meaning: A test assessing wear caused by rotating contact bodies.
Hardness derived from the relationship between a pyramidal indentation and load.

mfg1-surface-completion37-lesson-001.activity: 10 min: Organize five assessment targets. 10 min: Match tests with measured quantities. 7 min: List checks for two products with different color and wear requirements. 3 min: Explain examples versus acceptance limits.
safety: Compare purposes on paper; do not perform chemical-drop, irradiation, abrasion or voltage-application tests.
mfg1-surface-completion37-lesson-001.summary: Separate test names, assessed properties, conditions and limits. Do not reinterpret HV or typical values as guarantees of another property.

mfg1-surface-completion37-lesson-002.title: Distinguish analytical targets from reaction equations
mfg1-surface-completion37-lesson-002.objective: Distinguish sulfuric-acid acidity from sulfate ions, oxide classes and reaction-dependent concentration measures.

paragraphs.title: One sample, different measured quantities
paragraphs.text: A sample containing sulfuric acid may be assessed for acidity by neutralization titration or for sulfate by precipitation separation. One model of the latter is Ba²⁺ reacting with SO₄²⁻ to form sparingly soluble BaSO₄. Both may be called sulfuric-acid analysis, but their targets differ. Check interfering components and the specified method.

paragraphs.title: Check atoms and charges
paragraphs.text: In Ba²⁺＋SO₄²⁻→BaSO₄, the total charge on the left is zero and the product is neutral. Do not confuse superscript ion charges with subscripts counting atoms. Printing or text extraction may omit charges; do not treat such an equation as verified. This explains equation reading, not reagent-mixing instructions.

paragraphs.title: Classify oxides by reaction partners
paragraphs.text: Acidic oxides react with bases to form salts; basic oxides react with acids to form salts. Carbon dioxide and calcium oxide respectively illustrate these classes. Aluminum oxide and zinc oxide are amphoteric. Use verified basic concepts rather than memorizing reversed descriptions or mismatched names and formulas.

paragraphs.title: Names do not determine solution acidity or equivalents
paragraphs.text: The term acid salt refers to replaceable acid-derived hydrogen remaining in the formula; its solution is not necessarily acidic. Normality depends on the specified reaction and equivalents, not the substance name alone. Do not uniformly divide molarity by valence. Oxide reaction examples do not model every species or reaction in solution.

terms.meaning: Formation of a sparingly soluble solid in solution.
An oxide that reacts with a base to form a salt.
A quantity expressing matched reacting capacity for a specified reaction.

mfg1-surface-completion37-lesson-002.activity: 10 min: Diagram the two analytical targets. 10 min: Count atoms and charges on paper. 7 min: Compare oxide reaction partners. 3 min: Explain why names alone do not determine acidity or equivalents.
safety: Do not experiment with barium salts or other reagents. Follow qualification, training and the specified analytical method.
mfg1-surface-completion37-lesson-002.summary: Decide the quantity to determine first. Check charges, reaction partners and equivalent conditions separately.

mfg1-electrical-completion37-scope.title: Four separate oscilloscope specifications
mfg1-electrical-completion37-scope.objective: Explain channels, bandwidth, sampling and memory separately.

paragraphs.title: Simultaneous signals
paragraphs.text: Input channels determine how many signals can be observed together. Switching one input between two signals is not simultaneous observation of their timing. Check the required signals and available input conditions against specifications.

paragraphs.title: Bandwidth and sampling
paragraphs.text: Bandwidth concerns the speed of signals that can be observed; sampling rate concerns conversions to data per second. They are separate specifications. A large sampling rate does not remedy insufficient bandwidth.

paragraphs.title: Recording capacity
paragraphs.text: Memory stores acquired data. Fast sampling cannot provide the required waveform record if capacity is insufficient. Match observation duration and recording conditions. Probe suitability, input ratings and safe connections still require separate checks.

terms.reading: にゅうりょくちゃねるすう
terms.meaning: Number of inputs usable simultaneously.

terms.reading: しゅうはすうたいいき
terms.meaning: Frequency range relevant to observing fast signals.
Number of samples acquired per second.
Capacity for storing acquired data.

mfg1-electrical-completion37-scope.activity: Table the four specifications and explain simultaneous comparison and long recording requirements.
safety: Do not connect actual equipment from this lesson alone; check ratings and approved measurement procedures.
mfg1-electrical-completion37-scope.summary: Keep channels, bandwidth, sampling and memory separate.

mfg1-electrical-completion37-lcr.title: Follow LCR measurement information and calculations
mfg1-electrical-completion37-lcr.objective: Distinguish L/C/R from voltage, current and phase information used to calculate them.

paragraphs.title: Measured quantity
paragraphs.text: L is inductance, C capacitance and R resistance. LCR meters measure these and impedance. A displayed number needs its quantity, unit and measurement conditions to have meaning.

paragraphs.title: Information becomes a result
paragraphs.text: In the source’s auto-balancing bridge method, voltage, current and phase-difference information is digitized and processed to calculate LCR and impedance. The display is a method-based result, not terminal voltage merely renamed.

paragraphs.title: Method versus product specification
paragraphs.text: One method does not establish identical construction for all LCR meters. Historical comparisons do not prove current product difficulty or accuracy rankings. Check terminals, measurement frequency and range for the actual instrument and component.

terms.meaning: Quantity relating magnetic flux and current in coils.
Quantity describing ability to store charge.
Relative advance or delay between AC waveforms.

mfg1-electrical-completion37-lcr.activity: Sort L/C/R cards as target quantities and voltage/current/phase cards as measurement information.
safety: Do not infer terminal layouts or live connections from a conceptual method.
mfg1-electrical-completion37-lcr.summary: Separate target quantities from information used to calculate results.

mfg1-electrical-completion37-thermocoupl.title: Two temperatures in thermocouple measurement
mfg1-electrical-completion37-thermocoupl.objective: Explain dissimilar metals and temperature difference, including reference conditions and range.

paragraphs.title: Metals and measuring junction
paragraphs.text: Thermocouples use thermoelectric voltage from dissimilar metals for temperature measurement. If T1 is the measuring side and T2 the instrument side, handling T2 also affects the result. Metal color or shape alone does not determine temperature.

paragraphs.title: Reference side
paragraphs.text: Check reference handling and reference-junction compensation in the measurement-system specification. A two-metal/two-temperature sketch does not specify all wiring, compensation or polarity. Match type, polarity, compensation leads and instrument settings together.

paragraphs.title: Example ranges are not universal
paragraphs.text: Even K-type applicability depends on wire diameter, sheath, atmosphere and instrument. A textbook range does not authorize all K-type products. Verify the actual product for the intended temperature and conditions.

terms.meaning: Sensor using thermoelectric voltage from dissimilar metals.
Reference-side junction used to interpret thermoelectric voltage.
Specified leads connecting a thermocouple and instrument.

mfg1-electrical-completion37-thermocoupl.activity: Point to T1 and T2 and explain why both temperatures require consideration.
safety: Do not infer polarity or wiring from the principle sketch; follow approved equipment-specific procedures.
mfg1-electrical-completion37-thermocoupl.summary: Distinguish the reference side and product-specific range from the principle.

mfg1-electrical-completion37-light.title: Illuminance meters: detector versus measured quantity
mfg1-electrical-completion37-light.objective: Relate photodiode light conversion to illuminance measurement.

paragraphs.title: Converting light
paragraphs.text: An illuminance meter converts light reaching its detector into electrical information used to measure illuminance. The source names a photodiode. Separate the detector’s function from the final displayed quantity.

paragraphs.title: Light is not magnetic flux density
paragraphs.text: Illuminance and the magnetic flux density measured by gaussmeters are different. Electronic instruments are not interchangeable merely because both are electronic. Match the target quantity, instrument and detector; record instrument names with quantities.

paragraphs.title: Comparison conditions
paragraphs.text: Detector position, orientation and ambient light are measurement conditions. A location-dependent change is not immediate proof of lamp failure. Align conditions or record differences. A detector name does not guarantee calibration or accuracy.

terms.meaning: Instrument measuring illuminance at a light receiver.
Component converting light into electrical information.
Part receiving the light to be measured.

mfg1-electrical-completion37-light.activity: Sort illuminance meters and gaussmeters by light or magnetic target; explain position and orientation.
safety: Detector names do not specify terminals or ratings; follow the instrument specifications and verification method.
mfg1-electrical-completion37-light.summary: Relate light conversion to illuminance without confusing component and displayed quantity.

mfg1-electrical-completion37-hall.title: Match the three Hall-effect directions
mfg1-electrical-completion37-hall.objective: Separate perpendicular directions from polarity and terminal conditions.

paragraphs.title: Three directions
paragraphs.text: With current in a material and a magnetic field perpendicular to it, Hall voltage appears perpendicular to both. Read current, field and voltage as three directions, not one arrow.

paragraphs.title: Reading a flat sketch
paragraphs.text: If current is horizontal on the page and field perpendicular to the page, Hall voltage is vertical on the page. This does not universally determine which side is positive. Verify signs and terminals against the component specifications and conditions.

paragraphs.title: Detected quantity
paragraphs.text: Hall elements detect magnetic flux density and are used in gaussmeters. A voltage arrow is not an actual terminal specification. Match quantity, sensor orientation and specified conditions with a suitable measurement method.

terms.meaning: Voltage appearing perpendicular to current and magnetic field.
Directions meeting at right angles.
Magnetic quantity measured by gaussmeters and similar instruments.

mfg1-electrical-completion37-hall.activity: Match horizontal, vertical and out-of-page directions with current, Hall voltage and field; distinguish direction from polarity.
safety: Do not derive actual sensor connections or polarity from arrows alone.
mfg1-electrical-completion37-hall.summary: Separate perpendicular geometry from product-specific polarity and terminals.

mfg1-electrical-completion37-resistance.title: Resistance methods and measurement-system effects
mfg1-electrical-completion37-resistance.objective: Distinguish two method names and R=V/I; avoid universal error corrections.

paragraphs.title: Method names and scope
paragraphs.text: The source names bridge and voltage-drop methods for resistance. It does not provide detailed bridge construction or adjustment procedures; names alone do not authorize circuit assembly. Historical comparisons do not prove current prevalence or superiority.

paragraphs.title: Paper calculation
paragraphs.text: The voltage-drop method uses corresponding voltage V and current I to calculate R=V/I. For 0.30 V and 15 mA, convert 15 mA to0.015 A:0.30/0.015=20Ω. This calculation does not establish safe connections or the true resistance.

paragraphs.title: System versus target resistance
paragraphs.text: Supplies, instruments, wires and contacts can affect results. Do not always add or subtract one fixed correction. Check which voltage/current locations were measured and whether conditions match; assess effects with the specified method.

terms.meaning: One resistance method named in the source.
Method deriving resistance from measured voltage and current.
Instruments, supply, wiring and connections involved in a measurement.

mfg1-electrical-completion37-resistance.activity: Record method names, the paper R=V/I calculation and system effects in three columns.
safety: A correct calculation does not authorize wiring or energizing actual equipment.
mfg1-electrical-completion37-resistance.summary: Separate method, calculation and system effects; no universal correction.

mfg1-mechanical-completion37-lesson-001.title: Read sign shape, content and required action together
mfg1-mechanical-completion37-lesson-001.objective: Distinguish prohibition, warning, chemical and emergency-location signs.

paragraphs.title: Not color alone
paragraphs.text: Read shape, inner picture and words together: a red crossed circle prohibits; a yellow triangle warns. No entry is not permission to enter carefully; electrical warning announces danger. Compare learning sketches with official workplace signs.

paragraphs.title: Chemical diamonds differ
paragraphs.text: Red chemical diamonds differ by flame, corrosion, health, environment or exclamation pictograms. They are not general prohibition circles. One symbol cannot identify every hazard or PPE choice; check label precautions and SDS.

paragraphs.title: Location and route
paragraphs.text: Extinguishers, AEDs and evacuation signs identify what is where. Distinguish evacuation buildings, open areas and tsunami locations. Knowing a sign does not establish safety or authority for firefighting/rescue. Follow reporting, evacuation and emergency procedures.

terms.meaning: Sign identifying a prohibited act.
Sign announcing danger or a need for caution.

mfg1-mechanical-completion37-lesson-001.activity: Annotate three model signs with prohibited acts, hazards and references; explain emergency routes on a paper plan.
safety: Do not remove unclear signs or recreate hazards.
mfg1-mechanical-completion37-lesson-001.summary: Combine shape, picture, words and location to choose action.

mfg1-mechanical-completion37-lesson-002.title: Read QC charts through axes and counting conditions
mfg1-mechanical-completion37-lesson-002.objective: Connect seven QC tools with original data.

paragraphs.title: Bars and cumulative line
paragraphs.text: For12 scratches,6 dimensional defects and2 dirt defects, total20, descending Pareto bars give cumulative60%,90%,100%. Separate count and percentage axes; match period and defect-counting rules.

paragraphs.title: Variation versus time
paragraphs.text: Histograms show counts in ranges such as equal-width classes, not time sequence. Control charts plot time-ordered points against control lines. Control limits are not product specification limits; prescribed runs/trends may still need checking inside lines.

paragraphs.title: Relation versus cause
paragraphs.text: Scatter plots pair two variables; an apparent association does not establish causation. Cause-and-effect diagrams organize hypotheses, which records/investigation must test. Check sheets define items and counting; other graphs show trends or composition as appropriate.

terms.meaning: Share of total accumulated up to a given item.
Value interval used to group measurements.

mfg1-mechanical-completion37-lesson-002.activity: Plot20 defects and60/90/100%; explain information retained by histograms versus control charts.
safety: Do not release products or alter conditions from chart appearance alone.
mfg1-mechanical-completion37-lesson-002.summary: Check axes, period and counting; separate correlation and cause.

mfg1-mechanical-completion37-lesson-003.title: Distinguish instrument shape, reference and graduation
mfg1-mechanical-completion37-lesson-003.objective: Differentiate supports, screw instruments, comparators and limit gauges.

paragraphs.title: Supporting versus measuring
paragraphs.text: Straightedges, squares, calipers, surface gauges, blocks and magnetic bases guide, transfer or hold in different ways. The source V-block has a90°groove supporting cylinders. Do not generalize90°to every block; verify specification and contact.

paragraphs.title: Micrometer rotation
paragraphs.text: Outside micrometers measure between fixed anvil and moving spindle. Pitch0.5mm/50divisions or1mm/100both yield0.01mm. Sleeve14.5mm plus thimble0.23mm gives14.73mm. Estimated digits are not guaranteed accuracy.

paragraphs.title: Comparison and acceptance
paragraphs.text: Plunger probes move linearly, lever probes tilt, and bore gauges compare internal diameter. Reference30.000mm with−0.012mm deviation gives29.988mm. Plug/snap limit gauges judge specified go/no-go conditions rather than display precise actual dimensions. Thread plugs check internal threads; rings external threads.

terms.meaning: Fixed measuring part of an outside micrometer.
Measurement deriving dimension from difference to a reference.

mfg1-mechanical-completion37-lesson-003.activity: Calculate graduations for both pitches; identify probes/references and distinguish go/no-go from numerical measurement.
safety: Do not adjust equipment without permission; follow measuring force, reference and temperature conditions.
mfg1-mechanical-completion37-lesson-003.summary: Relate shape to purpose; distinguish rotation/graduation and reference/deviation.

mfg1-mechanical-completion37-lesson-004.title: Caliper parts and hardness-indent reading positions
mfg1-mechanical-completion37-lesson-004.objective: Match parts with lines and directions used in hardness tests.

paragraphs.title: Caliper measuring parts
paragraphs.text: External jaws measure diameter/thickness, internal jaws internal diameter, and depth bar depth. The slider moves along the main scale; vernier readings use coincident lines. Slider, internal measuring surface and depth bar are different names.

paragraphs.title: Outline and reading length
paragraphs.text: The Vickers model is approximately square viewed from above; two opposite-corner lines are diagonals, not edges. Check both directions by the specified method. Knoop’s elongated diamond uses its long diagonal. Similar outlines do not authorize substitution of tests or loads.

paragraphs.title: Other quantities
paragraphs.text: Rockwell involves indentation depth, Brinell ball-indent diameter and Shore rebound height. Hardness is not tensile strength itself. Record symbols and conditions. Product damage and release decisions require separate judgment even for small indents.

terms.meaning: Caliper part moving along the main scale.
Line connecting nonadjacent corners of a quadrilateral.

mfg1-mechanical-completion37-lesson-004.activity: Point to three caliper measuring locations; draw two square diagonals and the elongated diamond’s long diagonal.
safety: Do not measure moving products; handle indented products according to specified decisions.
mfg1-mechanical-completion37-lesson-004.summary: Distinguish measuring surfaces, diagonals, depth, diameter and rebound for each purpose.

mfg1-mechanical-completion37-lesson-005.title: Drawing scales and nine line roles
mfg1-mechanical-completion37-lesson-005.objective: Separate scale examples from line patterns and widths.

paragraphs.title: Scale and actual size
paragraphs.text: Source enlargement examples are2:1,5:1,10:1,20:1,50:1; reductions1:2,1:5,1:10,1:20,1:50,1:100,1:200,1:500,1:1000,1:2000,1:5000,1:10000. Dimensions generally state actual size; printing magnification does not authorize changing them.

paragraphs.title: Widths and patterns
paragraphs.text: The thin/thick/extra-thick1:2:4ratio differs from pen examples0.3/0.5/0.7mm, which are not1:2:4. Read thick continuous outlines, thin dimension/extension lines and dashed hidden lines by their functions.

paragraphs.title: Other lines
paragraphs.text: Distinguish chain centerlines, double-chain phantom lines, wavy/zigzag breaks, cutting-plane lines and section hatching. Thin continuous lines can serve different roles. If copying/reduction obscures them, check the original.

terms.meaning: Reference line for adjacent parts or another moving position.
Line specifying a section cut and viewing direction.

mfg1-mechanical-completion37-lesson-005.activity: Match nine lines to samples; explain a12 dimension on a5:1 drawing.
safety: Do not machine from guessed unclear lines; confirm approved original and revision.
mfg1-mechanical-completion37-lesson-005.summary: Read scale, actual dimension, pattern and width separately.

mfg1-mechanical-completion37-lesson-006.title: Connect views, sections and dimensional limits
mfg1-mechanical-completion37-lesson-006.objective: Read projection and clearance intervals with examples.

paragraphs.title: View directions
paragraphs.text: In the original third-angle cuboid30wide×20high×12deep, front30×20, top30×12, right12×20. Top goes above front; right view goes right, with aligned dimensions. Check projection symbols/notes on real drawings rather than infer solely from layout.

paragraphs.title: Section material and dimensions
paragraphs.text: Separate cut material from hollow space; do not hatch holes as material. Full, half and partial sections show different extents. Dimension lines show measurement direction; extension lines project from ends. A section drawing is not permission to cut the product.

paragraphs.title: Compare intervals
paragraphs.text: For shaft19.96–19.98mm and hole20.00–20.03mm, minimum clearance20.00−19.98=0.02mm, maximum20.03−19.96=0.07mm. Explain positive clearance numerically; do not rank fits solely by letters without limits.

terms.meaning: Planar view projected from a specified direction.
Upper and lower permitted dimensional values.

mfg1-mechanical-completion37-lesson-006.activity: Match three cuboid views; distinguish hole/material and calculate minimum/maximum clearance.
safety: Original examples do not authorize actual machining or assembly.
mfg1-mechanical-completion37-lesson-006.summary: Match view, cut material, measurement direction and permitted intervals.

mfg1-mechanical-completion37-lesson-007.title: Read leaders, surface texture and welding instructions
mfg1-mechanical-completion37-lesson-007.objective: Distinguish targets and scope of radius, diameter, thickness, holes, roughness and welds.

paragraphs.title: Leader target
paragraphs.text: R may mean arc radius, diameter symbols diameter, t thickness. Read hole method/depth/through notes with their target. Parenthesized reference dimensions are not independent machining requirements; follow leaders to the correct face/hole.

paragraphs.title: More than a roughness value
paragraphs.text: Read material-removal requirements, Ra/Rz parameter, value and target surface. Do not silently replace the source Ra3.1μm. For an original Ra≤2.5μm instruction, check its surface and conditions. Smaller roughness is not always better.

paragraphs.title: Weld symbol shape and position
paragraphs.text: Separate reference line, arrow and basic symbol; distinguish I/V/bevel grooves from corner fillet welds. Under the source convention, a basic symbol above the line denotes the other side. Do not universalize this across drawing systems; verify standard/notes. Reading symbols does not authorize unqualified welding.

terms.meaning: Line linking a note to a particular location.
Prepared edge geometry for welding.

mfg1-mechanical-completion37-lesson-007.activity: Connect radius/diameter/thickness notes on an original plate; describe roughness surface and weld-symbol location.
safety: Do not change tools, settings or materials from symbols alone without authorization.
mfg1-mechanical-completion37-lesson-007.summary: Check the target and applicable drawing system, not just symbol names.

mfg1-mechanical-completion37-lesson-008.title: Match steel designation and machine parts to specifications
mfg1-mechanical-completion37-lesson-008.objective: Distinguish SS330 and lathe/mill/drill part names.

paragraphs.title: Numbers are not authorization
paragraphs.text: The source reads SS330 as an example of tensile strength at least330N/mm², not yield strength or allowable load330. Confirm standard edition, size category, certificate and use requirements; designation alone cannot approve design/acceptance.

paragraphs.title: Lathe parts
paragraphs.text: Identify headstock, chuck, tool post, tailstock and carriage. Saddle and apron relate to carriage; apron is not a chuck jaw. Layout is model-specific; learn actual controls from that machine’s instructions and training.

paragraphs.title: Rotating-tool machines
paragraphs.text: A vertical mill example has head, spindle, column, panel, table and bed. Drill examples distinguish column, chuck, drill, table, base and spindle handle. Machining centers exchange tools automatically, but axes and accessible faces depend on model and workholding.

terms.meaning: Lathe-carriage-related component identified by its model drawing.
Part containing operating controls and displays.

mfg1-mechanical-completion37-lesson-008.activity: Label original diagrams; separate what steel numbers tell you from specifications still requiring checks.
safety: A name diagram is not an operating procedure; do not touch parts on running equipment.
mfg1-mechanical-completion37-lesson-008.summary: Relate names/numbers/positions to specifications separately from authority.

mfg1-surface-completion37-lesson-003.title: Match reading position and conditions for temperature, density and color
mfg1-surface-completion37-lesson-003.objective: Explain sensor types, density conversion, menisci and indicators.

paragraphs.title: Sensor versus control equipment
paragraphs.text: Thermocouples use dissimilar-metal thermoelectric voltage; platinum resistance sensors use temperature-dependent resistance. Liquid-column thermometers read expansion. Separate measuring principles from heating/cooling equipment. Names such as cooling coil, external heat exchanger or immersion heater do not establish materials, chemical resistance or permissible conditions.

paragraphs.title: Conditions before concentration conversion
paragraphs.text: Hydrometers read their floating position. Density/concentration relationships depend on substance, temperature and calibration; do not borrow another liquid’s curve. In the specified fictitious linear model1.10→180g/L and1.14→220g/L,1.12→200g/L. This is not a conversion table for real liquids.

paragraphs.title: No universal upper/lower meniscus rule
paragraphs.text: The source hydrometer example reads the upper meniscus; transparent-liquid burette and volumetric-pipette examples use the lower meniscus at the mark. Confirm instrument, visibility, calibration and specified method; neither always upper nor always lower. Keep eyes level to prevent parallax.

paragraphs.title: Read color with indicator identity
paragraphs.text: Phenolphthalein changes colorless/red, methyl orange red/yellow, BTB yellow/green/blue. Their transition ranges differ. Colorless does not always mean neutral; red does not mean acidic with every reagent. Match indicator to reaction/endpoint; read pH strips against their product chart and conditions.

terms.meaning: Curved liquid surface caused by interaction with vessel walls.

terms.reading: はっきんていこうたい
terms.meaning: Sensor using temperature-dependent platinum resistance.
Appearance or change of color under particular conditions.

mfg1-surface-completion37-lesson-003.activity: 10min: Classify sensors/control equipment.10min: Calculate1.12in the model.7min: Explain menisci/indicators.3min: Explain risks of universal color judgments.
safety: No heater insertion, tank work, sampling or titration demonstrations; organize procedure checks on paper.
mfg1-surface-completion37-lesson-003.summary: Align principle, reading position, conversion conditions and indicator; do not reuse fictional conversion for real liquid.

mfg1-surface-completion37-lesson-004.title: Match alloy families, jig materials and conversion coatings
mfg1-surface-completion37-lesson-004.objective: Match principal constituents and process roles without judging suitability from names alone.

paragraphs.title: Copper/aluminum alloy names
paragraphs.text: Brass mainly pairs Cu/Zn, bronze Cu/Sn, cupronickel Cu/Ni. Duralumin is an Al/Cu/Mg/Mn family; ADC12is a die-casting example containing Al/Si/Cu. These are main-element correspondences, not composition ratios or guarantees for all grades.

paragraphs.title: Forming and weldability
paragraphs.text: Die casting forces molten metal into a die. Casting and wrought applications differ. Aluminum-alloy grade, heat treatment, shape and joining method affect conditions. Do not label all duralumin casting material or all aluminum alloys unweldable.

paragraphs.title: Jig roles
paragraphs.text: Examples include phosphor bronze, stainless steel, aluminum and titanium. Consider strength, current conduction, bath compatibility and contacts together. Chlorinated-rubber/fluorine coatings can reduce unwanted deposits, but must not insulate necessary electrical contacts. Names do not guarantee resistance to every acid/base.

paragraphs.title: Phosphate is not one recipe
paragraphs.text: Zinc, iron, manganese and calcium phosphate are conversion-coating families. Choose by corrosion protection, paint adhesion, lubrication and substrate. Family names do not authorize concentration, temperature, duration or later steps. A suitable pretreatment does not automatically match every paint/drying condition.

terms.meaning: Copper-alloy family principally combining copper/nickel.
Forming by forcing molten metal into a die.
Forming a different surface film through substrate chemical reaction.

mfg1-surface-completion37-lesson-004.activity: 10min: Match alloys/elements.10min: List holding/conduction/chemical checks.7min: Classify four phosphate families and purposes.3min: List conditions names cannot determine.
safety: Do not replace jigs, strip coatings, melt metal or adjust baths; compare approved material lists/specifications.
mfg1-surface-completion37-lesson-004.summary: Names begin the check; verify grade, jig role, coating purpose and process conditions.

mfg1-surface-completion37-lesson-005.title: Compare buff and abrasive families by finishing purpose
mfg1-surface-completion37-lesson-005.objective: Distinguish six buff families and abrasive names without selecting by color/grit alone.

paragraphs.title: Hardness and shape retention
paragraphs.text: Sisal uses relatively hard fibers, an example for coarse polishing/scratch removal. Cotton/flannel are softer intermediate/finishing families. Compressed-wool felt retains shape for detail polishing. Density, stitching and geometry vary even within families; names do not fix removal rate.

paragraphs.title: Soft families differ
paragraphs.text: Wool uses soft fibers; sponge conforms to curves. Rayon is synthetic fiber combining uniformity, softness and stiffness. Examples do not guarantee all wool/sponge stays cool. Match substrate, plating, scratches and target finish to approved tools.

paragraphs.title: Common names versus composition
paragraphs.text: Source examples associate sizer/lime/white bars with alumina, red bars/Danji with silica, green bars with chromium oxide. Red bar can also mean iron-oxide products. Names/colors do not establish ingredients. Verify product identification, SDS, particles, binder and suitable materials; no universal present-product formulation is guaranteed.

paragraphs.title: Earlier scratches and final evaluation
paragraphs.text: Fine stages do not necessarily remove remaining coarse scratches. Grit class is not a guaranteed Ra conversion. Solid/liquid abrasives differ in supply and spatter conditions. Record tool, abrasive, preceding step and evaluated face. Never clean/adjust rotating tools; follow specified stop/isolation for abnormalities.

terms.meaning: Buff material made from relatively hard natural fibers.
Compressed and bonded wool or similar material.
Particles acting on a surface for removal/finishing.

mfg1-surface-completion37-lesson-005.activity: 10min: Classify six families.10min: Match names to ingredient checks.7min: Choose checks for preceding scratches.3min: Explain limits of colors/grit.

mfg1-surface-completion37-lesson-006.title: Read control items and abnormalities in independent records
mfg1-surface-completion37-lesson-006.objective: Separate method, frequency and response from classifications, cumulative shares and limits.

paragraphs.title: Four questions
paragraphs.text: Paper example: appearance check; foreign deposits; specified lighting/limit sample; at lot start/after change; segregate affected goods and notify supervisor if abnormal. Read what/how/when/response separately. Do not skip frequency for convenience or fabricate records afterward. This is not a workplace standard.

paragraphs.title: Check sheet to priorities
paragraphs.text: Fictitious day:12foreign matter,6uneven color,4scratches,2others,total24. Foreign matter50%; first two cumulative75%. Read Pareto counts and cumulative line separately.50%of classified defects does not mean half all products defective. Check denominator/period.

paragraphs.title: Distribution, time and relation
paragraphs.text: Histograms show frequency intervals, control charts time sequence, scatterplots paired quantities. Cause-and-effect diagrams organize candidates, not proven causes. Do not infer causation from association or occurrence time from a distribution lacking order.

paragraphs.title: Process versus acceptance
paragraphs.text: Paper specification20–30,control23–26:26.8is within specification but above control limit. Product rejection and process investigation are separate. Follow abnormality/affected-product procedures; do not widen limits to conceal the change.

terms.meaning: Ordered accumulated counts divided by total.

mfg1-surface-completion37-lesson-006.activity: 10min: Separate item/method/frequency/response.10min: Calculate24-case shares.7min: Read26.8against both limits.3min: Explain chart purposes.
safety: Do not transfer fictional values/frequencies into real equipment settings or product judgments.
mfg1-surface-completion37-lesson-006.summary: Check denominator, period, quantity and order; separate control/specification and candidate/proven cause.

mfg1-surface-completion37-lesson-007.title: Report small abnormalities and pollution pathways
mfg1-surface-completion37-lesson-007.objective: Organize footing, handling, evacuation, emissions, noise and subsidence facts.

paragraphs.title: Record before harm escalates
paragraphs.text: For work/commuting injury, record time, place and work/travel conditions and follow company reporting. Formal recognition is determined separately from facts; do not omit reporting based on your own exclusion. Near misses still matter. Source accident ratios are not universal workplace probabilities.

paragraphs.title: Feet, suspended loads and evacuation
paragraphs.text: Safety shoes protect against certain foot hazards, not every load/chemical. Handling requires weight, shape, routes, aids and team needs, not lifting technique alone. Stay out from under suspended loads. For hot/dusty processes check enclosures/extraction and specified PPE. Verify routes/locations beforehand; knowing AED location does not replace decisions/training.

paragraphs.title: Air pollution and odor
paragraphs.text: SOx/NOx contribute to acid rain; VOC/NOx in sunlight form ozone and other photochemical oxidants. Odors may involve ammonia/sulfur compounds. Weak odor does not prove harmlessness; do not sniff closely. Gas scrubbers control gases but fans can cause noise: manage both.

paragraphs.title: Vibration versus subsidence
paragraphs.text: Machine vibration differs from ground sinking. Source examples include groundwater over-pumping shrinking clay and earthquake liquefaction. Report time, equipment, duration and location of unusual noise/vibration/sinking. Do not independently stop extraction or alter groundwater/equipment settings; involve responsible investigators.

terms.meaning: Dangerous event that did not become an accident.

terms.reading: こうかがくおきしだんと
terms.meaning: Oxidants such as ozone formed by sunlight-driven reactions.
Sinking of the ground surface.

safety: Never enter beneath suspended loads or bring your face near chemicals to smell. Follow emergency training/procedures for first aid and stopping equipment.
mfg1-surface-completion37-lesson-007.summary: Record/report conditions; one countermeasure must not create another hazard.

mfg1-surface-completion37-lesson-008.title: Separate coating, electron and painting models
mfg1-surface-completion37-lesson-008.objective: Distinguish corrosion/anodizing models and deposition, electrodeposition and curing; sketches are not wiring/recipes.

paragraphs.title: Metal versus solution
paragraphs.text: Local-cell corrosion involves metal contact/surface differences and electrolyte. Electrons travel through conductive metal paths; ions transport charge in solution. Pinholes let water reach substrate. Reactivity order alone cannot predict all corrosion rates/acid dissolution; consider films, liquid and temperature.

paragraphs.title: Two anodized-film regions
paragraphs.text: Typical porous films have pore-containing regions and a dense substrate-side barrier layer. Cell/pore sketches do not guarantee every film’s geometry. Natural oxide does not mean inert to every acid/base and differs from treated films. Coatings, electrical protection and material corrosion resistance are distinct strategies.

paragraphs.title: Equations as role models
paragraphs.text: Al→Al³⁺＋3e⁻shows oxidation/electron loss;2H⁺＋2e⁻→H₂reduction/gain. Simplified water/oxide equations do not describe every solution species/mechanism. Verify missing superscript charges against trusted sources. Electron arrows are not liquid electron paths or actual wiring.

paragraphs.title: Deposition and curing differ
paragraphs.text: Electrostatic painting uses charge forces, not a universal instruction to wire every substrate to positive power. Anionic/cationic electrodeposition assigns workpiece electrodes differently. Powder painting deposits powder and forms film with heating; baking heats to cure. Resin/water/solvent/one-/two-pack names do not determine durability rankings or mixing/temperature settings.

terms.meaning: Potential differences between small regions acting like a cell.
Dense substrate-side layer in typical anodized films.
Painting that forms film on a workpiece using an electric field.

mfg1-surface-completion37-lesson-008.activity: 10min: Draw metal electrons versus solution ions.10min: Locate electrons in half-reactions.7min: Classify electrostatic/electrodeposition/powder/baking.3min: List real conditions models cannot specify.
safety: Do not demonstrate electrode connections, bath mixing, gas production, paint mixing or heating. Follow specified materials, equipment, training and procedures.
mfg1-surface-completion37-lesson-008.summary: Models separate concepts; do not confuse charge, transport path, method and real conditions.
